target_customer: Startups and developers who need to add SMS texting to their apps and want fast carrier registration
problem: After carrier compliance changes, registering to send texts through Twilio and similar APIs takes weeks, which blocks new startups from launching messaging features.
business_model: Usage-based API with monthly plans ($5, $20, $100, $250 and up) that include usage credit

founders.name: Dennis Beatty
founders.background_notes: Principal engineer over payments at Entrata; early engineer and messaging tech lead at Podium, where he led an SMS payments product (YC page).

founders.name: Brett Beatty
founders.background_notes: Six years at Podium as senior engineer on Phones and account structure; brother of Dennis; the pair had a combined 11 years at Podium.

competitors.name: Telnyx
competitors.what: Messaging API marketing faster 10DLC registration approvals
competitors.traction_then: Not stated; made 10DLC registration mandatory with carriers blocking unregistered traffic from December 2024

technical_complexity.rationale: Building on carrier and aggregator connections plus compliance workflows is standard engineering, with hard parts in carrier registration and deliverability.

defensibility.rationale: Larger providers (Twilio, Telnyx, Sinch, Plivo) offer the same service, and Surge's edge was onboarding speed and support, which are copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors were all promoting faster approvals in 2024 to 2025 vendor content; no acquisition or shutdown of Surge was found.

market_need_then: Carrier A2P 10DLC rules were enforced by all three carriers after late 2023, and developers reported registration delays of weeks; Surge's own launch post cites 2 to 3 weeks with other providers.

branding.domain_note: Uses surge.app, not surge.com; the .app domain is in use for the company site and docs.

identity.logo: Not described in sources; the YC launch post uses a lightning bolt emoji
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, friendly, a little playful; the site tagline is The SMS API that actually cares about Developers and code samples use a Dominic Toretto movie quote

branding.community_and_virality: Founders Pack newsletter essay and a YC launch post; no merch or community found. The Surge name is shared with several unrelated companies, including a 2016 Uber pricing app.

brand_strength.rationale: Developer friendly voice and a memorable Stripe analogy, but the name is generic and shared with many other products.

outcome_analysis: Surge is a three person company from the Fall 2024 batch that sells an SMS API with fast carrier registration, built by two brothers who spent a combined 11 years at Podium. It is active and plans RCS and WhatsApp, but funding, revenue and customer traction are not public. Its edge depends on onboarding speed in a market where Twilio, Telnyx and others compete, so the outcome is still open.
notes: Funding seen only in aggregators: VCBacked and FundedIQ list a $500K pre-seed in December 2024, StartupIntros shows other conflicting figures ($11.5M total, $3M in 2022, $1.8M in Oct 2024) that may belong to other Surge companies. None are recorded as rounds. Only one dated competitor was found; Twilio is named by the company but without a dated source. No outcome news found since launch. name_qualities value descriptive was not used. Completeness pass: the $500K pre-seed (2024-12) is recorded from VCBacked alone; a cross-check search found no press or filing confirming it, and the conflicting StartupIntros figures remain unrecorded.
